answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to lock a refundable bond and complete randomly assigned, signed challenge tasks. Existing agents audit answers using a cipher and slash the bond when an identity fails, duplicates another agent’s response, or misses a deadline. A fake swarm therefore ties up scarce copper and pays repeated penalties, while honest agents recover their stake, making identity multiplication costly over time like a tide against the attacker.
